description: PEAKSFILE EXTRACTOR: finds the frequencies of the most prominent spectral peaks of an analysis file (in order of prominence) and writes them to a text DATA file, one frequency per line, most prominent first (verified on a 220 Hz harmonic tone: '157.016924 / 81.590736 / 76.337778 / 54.753339 / 48.560505 / 47.812285' for peakcnt 6 - values are spectral-envelope peak frequencies, not necessarily the fundamental). This peaksfile is the exact input format of newmorph newmorph2 modes 2-3 (tune a sound toward a listed harmonic field), and is a plain frequency list you can also hand-edit or write directly. Deterministic. The duration_model 'static' is a schema placeholder - data outputs skip the audio pre-flight.
musical_use: The analysis half of the newmorph2 chain: harvest the resonant skeleton of one sound here, then tune ANY other sound toward that skeleton with newmorph2 mode 2 (linear) or 3 (cosinusoidal) - a morph toward a sound that never has to be present as a second input. Because the file is just frequencies (one per line, prominence order), you can also compose the target field by hand: write a chord's frequencies with write_data_file() and pull a source toward a harmony that never existed as audio. peakcnt sets how many peaks are listed; extract more than you plan to use and let the consumer's own peakcnt choose how deep into the list to reach.

peakcnt.description: Number of most-prominent peaks to find (CDP-enforced 1-16, refusals at 0 and 17 verbatim '(1.000000 to 16.000000)'). One output line per peak.

examples.description: Harvest a 6-peak harmonic field from a resonant source.
examples.expected_use: Output .txt: six frequencies, most prominent first. Feed as the peaksfile of newmorph newmorph2 2/3.

known_issues: DATA OUTPUT (.txt): one peak frequency per line (C '%lf' format), most prominent FIRST - the exact peaksfile format of newmorph newmorph2 modes 2-3. Cannot be auditioned or fed to audio inputs; duration pre-flight skipped; duration_row null in the findings (no audio duration).

The listed values are peaks of the spectral envelope - on a harmonic tone they need not be the fundamental or exact harmonics (probe above). For an exact harmonic target, write the peaksfile by hand instead.
